config.title: Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals

intro.title: Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, accessible Angular component for a user profile card. You'll learn the core concepts of web accessibility (a11y), focusing on semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, and ARIA attributes. The main technologies involved are Angular templates, TypeScript, and built-in HTML accessibility features. By the end, you'll understand how to make your Angular applications usable for everyone, including people using assistive technologies.
intro.usecase: Accessibility fundamentals are essential for building inclusive web applications used by millions, such as public service portals, banking dashboards, and e-commerce sites. Developers implement a11y features like semantic HTML, ARIA attributes, and keyboard navigation in common UI components—forms for user registration, data tables in admin panels, interactive filters for product searches, and modal dialogs for confirmations. Mastering these practices ensures all users, including those relying on screen readers or keyboard-only input, can effectively interact with your application, meeting legal standards and expanding your product's reach.

objectives: Implement semantic HTML elements within Angular components to improve screen reader navigation
Apply ARIA attributes to Angular templates for enhanced assistive technology support
Configure keyboard navigation handlers for interactive Angular components
Bind accessible form controls with proper labels and validation announcements
Initialize focus management strategies for dynamic content updates in Angular applications
Render accessible color contrast and text scaling in Angular component styles
Integrate screen reader testing tools into the Angular development workflow

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from Angular core
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbol name and the module path in quotes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, enabling component creation and common directives.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported one of the required modules. Make sure to import both Component and CommonModule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Check that you're importing Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.

steps.title: Create the main AppComponent class
steps.instruction: Create the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator and define the component metadata including selector, standalone, imports, and template.
steps.hint:
Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define your component class. Set selector to 'app-root', standalone to true, imports to [CommonModule], and template to a simple placeholder like '

Accessibility Fundamentals

'.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Create the AppComponent class here with @Component decorator
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined with proper Angular component metadata.
successCriteria: AppComponent class exists with @Component decorator containing selector: 'app-root', standalone: true, imports: [CommonModule], and a template string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your @Component decorator includes all required metadata: selector, standalone, imports, and template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent class isn't properly defined. Check that you're using the @Component decorator with the correct metadata properties.

steps.title: Initialize component state with accessibility data
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, define an interface named AccessibilityItem with properties: id (number), title (string), and description (string).
steps.hint: Define the interface first, then create a property in the class with type annotation and initial value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a typed data structure representing accessibility guidelines, ready for display in the template.
successCriteria: AccessibilityItem interface is defined with id, title, and description properties. accessibilityItems property is declared with proper type and initialized with sample data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both the interface definition and property initialization are complete with proper types.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's review: define an interface with three properties, then create a class property with that type and initial data.

steps.title: create a property named accessibilityItems of
steps.instruction: create a property named accessibilityItems of type AccessibilityItem[] and initialize it with at least two sample items.
steps.hint: Define the interface first, then create a property in the class with type annotation and initial value.
steps.feedbackPartial: Review the instruction and try again.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Create the component template structure
steps.instruction: Inside the @Component decorator's template property, add a main container with a heading that says 'Accessibility Fundamentals'.
steps.hint: Use the <main> element for the main container and an <h1> element for the heading.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will have a semantic main container with an accessibility-focused heading.
successCriteria: The template property contains a <main> element with an <h1> element inside it displaying 'Accessibility Fundamentals'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the <main> container and <h1> heading with the correct text.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the template structure inside the @Component decorator with a <main> element containing an <h1>.

steps.title: Add semantic HTML elements for navigation
steps.instruction: Inside the component's template, add a <nav> element with an aria-label attribute set to 'Main navigation'.
steps.hint: The <nav> element should be placed directly in the template. Use double quotes for the aria-label value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of a semantic navigation element
<nav aria-label="Site navigation">
  <!-- Navigation links would go here -->
</nav>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now includes a semantic <nav> element with proper ARIA labeling for accessibility.
successCriteria: The template contains a <nav> element with aria-label="Main navigation"
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a <nav> element, but it's missing the aria-label attribute. Add aria-label="Main navigation" to make it fully accessible.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain a properly labeled <nav> element. Add <nav aria-label="Main navigation"> to the template.

steps.title: Implement accessible list structure
steps.instruction: Inside the component template, add an unordered list (<ul>) element with the ARIA role attribute set to 'list' and a list of accessibility items.
steps.hint: Use Angular's *ngFor directive to iterate over the accessibilityItems array and create list items (<li>) for each item.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Accessible list structure
  • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will contain an unordered list with proper ARIA role and dynamic list items.
successCriteria: The template includes a <ul> element with role="list" and uses *ngFor to render <li> elements for each accessibility item.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to include both the ARIA role and the *ngFor directive for the list items.
steps.feedbackWrong: The list structure is missing or incomplete. Check that you've added the <ul> with role="list" and used *ngFor to create the list items.

steps.title: Display accessibility items with ngFor
steps.instruction: Inside your template, use Angular's *ngFor directive to iterate through the accessibilityItems array and display each item's title and description in list items.
steps.hint: Add *ngFor="let item of accessibilityItems" to your <li> element, then use interpolation {{ item.title }} and {{ item.description }} to display the content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will dynamically render three list items, each showing an accessibility principle title and description.
successCriteria: The <li> element contains *ngFor directive that iterates through accessibilityItems and displays each item's title and description using interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using *ngFor with the correct syntax and displaying both the title and description properties from each item.
steps.feedbackWrong: The *ngFor directive isn't implemented correctly. Remember to use *ngFor="let item of accessibilityItems" on the <li> element and display item.title and item.description using {{ }} interpolation.

steps.title: Add accessible form controls
steps.instruction: Add a form element after the navigation section in your template, containing an accessible input field with proper label association and a submit button.
steps.hint: Use the <form> element, then add a <label> with 'for' attribute matching the input's 'id'. Include a submit button with type='submit'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Accessible form structure
<form>
  <label for="nameInput">Your Name:</label>
  <input id="nameInput" type="text">
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now includes a form with properly labeled input field and submit button, demonstrating accessible form controls.
successCriteria: Form element is added after navigation, contains label with 'for' attribute, input with matching 'id', and submit button with type='submit'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a form, but check that the label's 'for' attribute matches the input's 'id' exactly, and the button has type='submit'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form structure is missing or incomplete. Ensure you have a <form> element containing a <label> with 'for' attribute, an <input> with matching 'id', and a <button type='submit'>.

steps.title: Implement focus management
steps.instruction: Add tabindex='0' and a CSS class for focus styling to the navigation list items to make them keyboard-focusable.
steps.hint: Add tabindex='0' to each <li> element and include a class like 'focusable' that can be styled with outline or box-shadow.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example: making an element keyboard-focusable -->
<button tabindex='0' class='focusable'>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The list items will be keyboard-focusable with visual focus indicators when navigating with Tab.
successCriteria: Each <li> element in the *ngFor loop has tabindex='0' and a class attribute for styling focus.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added tabindex or a class, but both are needed for proper focus management.
steps.feedbackWrong: The list items are not keyboard-focusable. Add tabindex='0' and a class to each <li>.

steps.title: Add ARIA live regions for dynamic content
steps.instruction: Add an aria-live attribute to the navigation element to announce dynamic content changes to screen readers.
steps.hint: Use the aria-live attribute with a value of 'polite' or 'assertive' on the nav element.
steps.analogousExample: Dynamic content updates will be announced here.
steps.expectedOutcome: The navigation element will have an aria-live attribute to announce dynamic content changes.
successCriteria: The nav element includes an aria-live attribute with a valid value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to add the aria-live attribute directly to the nav element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding the aria-live attribute to the nav element in the template.
